# Vendored global themes: provenance and what was changed

All three upstreams are actively maintained and permissively licensed, which is
why they were chosen over authoring another theme ourselves (DN-28).

| Theme | Upstream | Pinned at | Licence | Last upstream activity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Catppuccin Mocha, Catppuccin Latte | github.com/catppuccin/kde | v0.4.0 | MIT | 2026-08-05 |
| Orchis Light | github.com/vinceliuice/Orchis-kde | main @ 2025-10-18 | GPL-3.0 | 2025-10-18 |
| Nordic | github.com/EliverLara/Nordic | main @ 2026-07-23 | GPL-3.0 | 2026-07-23 |
| Windows Modern (SP+ Windows 11 light/dark) | github.com/Jeysef/KDE-Windows-Modern | `7ef6bfe99a472f2fc7fa473383eda50f411a8840` | GPL-3.0 | see note below |

## Why these are not shipped verbatim

Every one of them was published incomplete as a Plasma 6 global theme. Verified in
the cycle35 guest on 2026-08-28:

- **All four packages named the Plasma 5 decoration plugin** (`org.kde.kwin.aurorae`).
  Plasma 6.7 needs `org.kde.kwin.aurorae.v2`. This is the same defect that made
  SP+ Calm silently fail to apply for a whole cycle.
- **None declared fonts**, so switching theme left the previous theme's type in place.
- **Nordic shipped no `metadata.json` at all**, only a Plasma 5 `metadata.desktop`,
  so Plasma 6 could not load it.
- **Catppuccin's package Id did not match its directory name**, and Plasma resolves
  a theme by Id: `plasma-apply-lookandfeel Catppuccin-Mocha` failed outright with
  "Unable to find the theme".
- **Dangling asset references.** Nordic named the icon theme `candy-Nordic-green`
  and a Plasma desktop theme it does not ship; Orchis named `Tela-circle` icons and
  `Vimix` cursors it does not ship. Each of those would leave that component
  unchanged on switch.
- **Orchis carried Plasma 5 tabbox keys** (`[kwinrc][DesktopSwitcher]`,
  `[WindowSwitcher]`) which our own theme gate rejects as unsafe.

## What we changed

`contents/defaults` was regenerated for each package so that every component key
is present and every value resolves to an asset the image actually installs, and
`metadata.json` was authored with `Id` equal to the directory name. Icon themes
were standardised on Papirus (packaged by Fedora, actively maintained) because it
is the only icon set that covers every theme without a dangling reference. Widget
style is Breeze for the vendored themes: Kvantum's active skin is stored outside
the look-and-feel package, so a Kvantum-styled theme cannot switch its own skin
and would leave the desktop half-changed.

Regenerated by `theme/tools/` and gated by `validate-global-themes.py`, which
fails the build if any of the above regresses.

## Windows Modern — provenance pinned 2026-08-30 (DN-43)

This row was **missing entirely** until DN-43's audit; the tree was vendored with no
recorded ref. The commit above was established after the fact by fetching upstream and
comparing, so it is a *reconstructed* pin, not a record made at vendoring time. What
that comparison did and did not prove, stated precisely:

- **Verified byte-identical at this commit:** the Aurorae, desktop-theme, colour-scheme,
  Kvantum and icon component trees, and `ATTRIBUTION-Windows-Modern.md`.
- **Deliberately divergent, not a mismatch:** the two look-and-feel packages. SP+ changes
  the package IDs to `org.secureprospective.spplus.windows11.{dark,light}`, regenerates
  `contents/defaults`, and ships its own layout scripts. Upstream `BUILD.md` and
  `patches/` are not vendored.
- **Not vendored at all:** upstream's custom C++ applets, panel template, session-lock
  shell and patched boot greeter (excluded at `images/kde/Containerfile:L860-L863`), and
  the upstream Windows Modern wallpaper.

Anyone re-vendoring must record the new ref here at the time of the update rather than
reconstructing it later.

## Cursor policy for Windows Modern (DN-43, decided 2026-08-30)

Upstream's dark package declares `Windows-modern-dark-cursors`, and **no such cursor
directory exists upstream** — the reference is dangling. `breeze_cursors` is therefore
substituted. This is a `REQUIRED-COMPAT` substitution, not an SP+ style preference: the
declared asset was never shipped, so DN-43's "the theme wins on everything it declares"
cannot apply to it.

Christopher decided on 2026-08-30 to **keep Breeze cursors and disclose it** rather than
source a third-party Windows-style cursor set, which would add a dependency subject to
the standing rule that anything shipping in SP+ must be actively maintained. The DN-44
preview change-list must therefore not imply the cursor changes.
